claims.claim: MPS sits in the AI/server infrastructure chain at power conversion and delivery: rising rack compute density increases the need for efficient, high-current power management, while Q2 2026 Enterprise Data revenue of $380.6M (+164.3% YoY) shows current company-level transmission.

The structural opportunity is broader than current core power sockets because MPS is sampling high-voltage AC-to-DC products for 800V data-center architectures, but architecture transitions can also shift where value accrues and create successor bottlenecks.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Power conversion is required infrastructure for higher-density compute, and current enterprise-data growth shows material exposure; evidence does not establish exclusive control.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: AI/server, communications, storage/computing, automotive and industrial exposures diversify demand, while Enterprise Data reached 38.8% of Q2 revenue and is increasingly important.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Power management remains necessary across architectures, but socket displacement, customer redesign, integration and competing suppliers can shift content and economics.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Management describes a diversified global supply chain, but semiconductor supplier capacity/yield dependence remains a structural constraint.

risks.risk: AI infrastructure demand can remain strong while MPS captures less value if power architectures integrate functions differently, competitors win sockets, or customer ramps change.
Supplier capacity and yield constraints can become a successor bottleneck as MPS expands capacity goals beyond $6B.

causalEdges.mechanism: higher rack power requires more sophisticated conversion, regulation and delivery
causalEdges.falsifier: new architectures materially reduce addressable MPS content per deployed compute unit

causalEdges.mechanism: socket wins convert deployed AI/server platforms into semiconductor shipments
causalEdges.falsifier: enterprise-data deployments rise while MPS revenue/content materially decouples

causalEdges.mechanism: high-voltage AC-to-DC sampling can extend MPS upstream in the power chain
causalEdges.falsifier: sampling fails to convert to production or alternate architectures/suppliers capture the layer

unknowns.unknown: Customer-specific AI/server concentration and socket share are not quantified in the reviewed evidence.
Primary-hosted filing/release lineage is still an Alpha/source-integrity gap; Beta conclusions use current company-origin syndication and an SEC-filing mirror without claiming primary-source closure.

claims.claim: Current operating evidence does not falsify the growth thesis: Q2 2026 revenue rose 47.6% YoY, operating margin reached 31.0%, and Enterprise Data rose 164.3% YoY, but the mix shift raises concentration and execution sensitivity.

Diluted weighted-average shares were 49.26M in Q2 2026 versus 48.02M in Q2 2025, while Q2 stock-based compensation and related expense was $53.5M; this is a measurable dilution/compensation pressure, not evidence of financing distress.
MPS's capacity expansion and >$6B capacity goal can improve resilience and capture demand, but it raises utilization risk if AI/server ordering normalizes or customers cancel/reschedule orders.

factors.name: thesisQuality
factors.basis: Exceptional current growth supports the thesis, while concentration, architecture substitution and a high execution bar remain material falsifiers.

factors.name: governancePower
factors.basis: Reviewed Beta evidence does not establish a complete current governance assessment.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Diversification efforts are positive, but supplier capacity/yield dependence and committed wafer exposure remain real semiconductor-chain risks.

risks.risk: Enterprise Data represented 38.8% of Q2 2026 revenue, increasing sensitivity to AI/server ordering patterns and major platform cycles.
Stock-based compensation and a higher diluted share count create shareholder dilution pressure even while earnings are growing rapidly.
Supplier capacity, wafer commitments, yield issues and customer cancellations can create inventory, margin or fulfillment stress during a demand transition.
AI TAM growth is not equivalent to durable MPS socket share, pricing power or content per system.

causalEdges.mechanism: a larger revenue share tied to enterprise-data ramps increases sensitivity to platform timing and capex cycles
causalEdges.falsifier: non-enterprise growth and customer diversification offset a material AI/server slowdown

causalEdges.mechanism: supplier commitments can outlast rescheduled or cancelled customer demand
causalEdges.falsifier: flexible sourcing and sustained broad demand keep utilization, inventory and margins resilient

unknowns.unknown: Exact top-customer concentration, current wafer-supplier concentration and contractual take-or-pay exposure are not established by reviewed Beta evidence.
No complete source-addressed current governance assessment is asserted.
